Transcribed from /tmp/ref/DS04_Farmer/Main.java (CFR decompile of the shipped Main.class). Mapping of synthetic names: bl/bl2/bl3/bl4 -> wolf/sheep/vegetable/farmer; n/n2 in searchWay -> start/last; loop cursor n in DFS -> index; arrayList/node/node2 in showResult -> result/now/next; stringBuilder -> sb; counter n in canConnect -> count.

Fidelity details preserved: node enumeration order is the 4-deep loop over {true, false} (wolf, sheep, vegetable, farmer) so indices match the original; isValid is `farmer == sheep || (wolf != sheep && sheep != vegetable)`; canConnect requires the farmer side to flip and at most one other item to move. In DFS the recursion reuses `startNode.flag` as the persistent scan cursor and resets it to 0 on backtrack — kept exactly. The decompiler's `if (node.flag != nodes.size()) continue;` guard is unreachable-by-construction (the inner while only exits when flag == size), so it is written as the equivalent positive `if (startNode.flag == nodes.size()) { ... break; }`; semantics are unchanged.

Correctness sanity check: the classic farmer/wolf/goat/cabbage puzzle has exactly 2 minimal solutions of 7 crossings each, and both printed solutions start and end with the goat ("带着羊"), never leave wolf+goat or goat+cabbage unattended, and end with all four on the far bank. Output diffs byte-identical against the untouched shipped Main.class/Node.class/Stack.class run from the module directory.
